sections.en:
Good evening, everyone. I am Milly. 
In a crowd, speaking up has never been my strong suit.
But if I had to describe myself in one sentence, 
I’d say: I am a "Brave Introvert.” 
I love exploring the world, even when the unknown can be scary.
Because a voice inside pushing me: 'Don’t just stay here. Go see the world!

sections.title: 段落 2
sections.label: Section 2
sections.cue: 請編輯本段，加入自己的關鍵字提示
sections.en:
On a solo trip to Japan, I stood on the glass walkway of the Akashi Kaikyō Bridge. 
when I looked straight down at the ocean waves.
My knees went weak.
I felt how small we’re against the vast sea. 
But even with my heart racing... I crossed that bridge alone.
Just as I reached the other side, I took out my phone to capture the beautiful sunset. 
That’s when an elderly Japanese man and his granddaughter approached me. 
They spoke so fast. 
I knew some Japanese... but in that moment, my mind went blank. 
I had so much to say... but nothing came out. 
So, I just smiled and nodded. 
But then, we communicated using translation apps, broken words, and big gestures. 
Surprisingly... we understood each other. 
He pointed to Shodoshima: “So beautiful... you must go!”

sections.label: Section 3
sections.cue: 請編輯本段，加入自己的關鍵字提示
sections.en:
I learned: Courage doesn't mean having no fear. 
It means... staying, even when you're scared.”
So instead of running away, I began following people who inspire me, like The DoDo Men and Lily Chen. 
They showed me what it means to be brave and explore the unknown.
When I saw Lily share her 10-year journey to get her Canadian visa. 
It wasn’t just her English that moved me— it was her persistence with open doors. 
And I started to dream: What if I could be that? 
To be in charge of my time. To be free to live anywhere.
I realized: Language isn’t just a tool—it is the key to my freedom.

sections.label: Section 4
sections.cue: 請編輯本段，加入自己的關鍵字提示
sections.en:
To be honest, I’m still a bit socially awkward. 
But I see it now… it’s not about perfect grammar. 
It’s about the courage to speak up, and the heart to connect with others. 
Fortunately, I met Spencer and Allison. 
Spencer invited me here, and Allison helped me clarify my path. 
Their warmth made me feel that Toastmasters is a 'safe stage.' 
It’s a place to fail, to practice, and finally... to find our voice.

sections.label: Section 5
sections.cue: 請編輯本段，加入自己的關鍵字提示
sections.en:
Standing on this stage now, 
I’m no longer hesitating. 
Besides improving my English, 
I’m here to learn how to speak with confidence. 
In the future, I want to be like you—to give warmth and support to others. 
I am still learning, But I believe: 
every step out of my comfort zone… is a step closer to my ideal life. Thank you.
